title: Quentin and the Visitor
premise: Felix Amberdale returns to the family estate to bury their twin brother Quentin, only to find the excavation crew has unearthed a door sealed from the inside beneath the old orchard. As night falls, Felix discovers Quentin may not be dead at all—or that something wearing Quentin's memories came home twelve years ago and was kept hidden by their mother's desperate bargains. Holding out until sunrise with the crew's survivors, Felix must choose between loyalty to the sibling they loved and the truth that what was invited in still expects its welcome. In the end, Felix unseals the door themselves, trading their own place in the world for the family's survival—and walks into the dark as dawn breaks.
about_author: L. M. Ishikawa is a former mortuary archivist who spent six years cataloguing unclaimed estates before turning to fiction. They write horror about houses that remember, and live quietly in a coastal town where they refuse to dig in their own garden.

chapters.title: The Wrong Sibling
chapters.summary: Felix arrives home for Quentin's funeral, greeted by a house that feels rehearsed for their return. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: grief tangled with guilt over twelve years of absence.

chapters.title: Open Casket, Closed Case
chapters.summary: At the viewing, Felix notices the body is wrong—the hands, the scar, the teeth. The funeral director deflects. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: creeping dread disguised as mourning.

chapters.title: The Orchard Crew
chapters.summary: Excavation for the new well strikes something; the foreman, Dara Okafor, shows Felix a stone door with no outside handle. POV: alternating Felix/Dara. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: Sealed From Within
chapters.summary: Dara's crew examines the door's hinges—rusted shut from the inside. That night, Felix hears footsteps upstairs matching Quentin's childhood gait. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: denial cracking.

chapters.title: Mother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix finds their mother's journals: payments, dates, and a recurring entry—'It stayed quiet this month.' The last entry is dated after Quentin's death. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: betrayal of the dead.

chapters.title: The First to Go
chapters.summary: A crew member, Pell, goes missing near the orchard; his tools are found arranged neatly by the door. Dara wants police; the phone lines are dead. POV: Dara. Emotional beat: professional calm fraying.

chapters.title: What Quentin Knew
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: twelve years ago, teenage Felix watched Quentin speak to something in the cellar and say nothing. POV: young Felix. Emotional beat: retroactive horror at their own silence.

chapters.title: Knocking
chapters.summary: The door knocks from inside—three times, the family's old signal. Felix answers aloud before thinking. The house lights die section by section. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the terrible intimacy of being recognized.

chapters.title: Barricade
chapters.summary: Felix and Dara fortify the kitchen as the remaining crew scatters or vanishes. They compare notes: the missing, the noises, the ledger. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: strangers becoming allies.

chapters.title: It Sounds Like Him
chapters.summary: Quentin's voice calls Felix by a private childhood nickname through the walls, recounting memories only the twins shared. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: love weaponized against reason.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: In the ledger's final pages, Felix finds the truth: their mother invited it in to replace Quentin after his drowning, and the bargain requires an Amberdale at every solstice. Tonight is the solstice. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: duty revealed as debt.

chapters.title: Dara's Price
chapters.summary: Dara admits she took the job because her own brother vanished on this land decades ago; she needs to see the door opened. POV: Dara. Emotional beat: two kinds of loyalty colliding.

chapters.title: The House Turns
chapters.summary: The house begins rearranging itself—hallways lengthening toward the cellar, windows showing the orchard at night regardless of hour. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: claustrophobia; home as trap.

chapters.title: Pell Returns
chapters.summary: Pell comes back wrong—smiling, wet, insisting everyone 'come meet him.' Dara locks him out; he scratches politely until dawn logic fails. POV: Dara. Emotional beat: horror of the polite dead.

chapters.title: Confession at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Felix tells Dara everything: the twin bond, the drowned boy, the suspicion they buried instead of investigated. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: catharsis; truth as the only weapon left.

chapters.title: The Bargain Offered
chapters.summary: The voice offers a trade: Quentin back, whole and warm, if Felix takes his place behind the door. It proves it can deliver—briefly, Quentin stands in the kitchen, alive, weeping. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: love against duty at full pressure.

chapters.title: Sunrise Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Dara calculates they cannot survive till dawn inside; the house is herding them cellarward. Their only options are the door or the fields, and the fields are worse. POV: Dara. Emotional beat: grim clarity.

chapters.title: Quentin's Choice
chapters.summary: The real Quentin, momentarily himself, begs Felix not to open the door—that he'd rather stay dead than be the thing's lure. POV: Quentin (fragmented). Emotional beat: sacrifice reframing twelve years of silence.

chapters.title: Unsealing
chapters.summary: Felix breaks the hinge seals with the family axe, choosing truth over the comfortable lie their mother built. The door opens onto a stairwell breathing like a throat. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: resolve amid terror.

chapters.title: Below
chapters.summary: Felix descends with Dara holding the light; they find Pell, the missing crew, and rows of Amberdales across generations—all preserved, all waiting. The thing offers Felix Quentin's life one final time. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the climax of temptation.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Felix refuses the swap but offers a third bargain: themselves as witness, not resident—bound to remember and tell, breaking the cycle of secrecy that fed it. The thing, starved of lies, accepts. Quentin's body finally rests. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: costly, imperfect victory.

chapters.title: Sunrise
chapters.summary: Dawn. Dara and Felix bury the door under collapsed earth and leave together, Felix carrying the ledger to publish the truth. The last line: somewhere below, three knocks—patient now, almost fond. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: grief, freedom, and the loyalty that survives truth.
